conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced, so p_up is 52 on a 6.5% absolute move, giving +0.26. A peer document puts Q3 alumina prices up 8%, the CFO was upbeat mid-quarter and the bar has been cut about 14% in 90 days, all leaning positive. Against that, LME aluminium is about 6% below its Q3 average so far in October, which feeds a Q4 outlook the stock trades on, and the last three prints fell 1.5-6.8%. The findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is about half that because this name has sold its last three prints, so the reaction function, not the fundamental read, sets p_up.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.49 on revenue $3.76B (8 analysts, range $0.85-$1.81, Alphastreet, https://news.alphastreet.com/alcoa-aa-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-1-49-reports-october-15/), $1.54 on $3.78B (Investing.com, 2026-10-15, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/alcoa-earnings-on-deck-can-aluminum-offset-alumina-weakness-93CH-4952041). Zacks consensus is $1.65 on $3.61B with a Most Accurate Estimate of $1.72 (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:e0488e589094b:0-alcoa-gears-up-to-post-q3-earnings-what-lies-ahead-for-the-stock/). TipRanks shows $1.27, but it carries a wrong report date. Two sources agree at about $1.49-1.54, so the bar is sourced but dispersed. One preview says consensus is down 13.9% over 90 days from $1.73. Prior quarter: $2.12 actual against about $2.25-2.35. The company gives no EPS guide. Its Q3 outlook is sequential and excludes price: alumina segment about +$10M, aluminum segment flat, alumina costs in the aluminum segment -$10M, Section 232 tariff -$10M on volume only, operational tax $80-90M (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001675149/000119312526306118/aa-ex99_1.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest is 11.7M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement with 2.9 days to cover; it was 12.0M (3.5 days) on 09-15, 12.2M on 08-31, 10.9M on 08-14 and about 8.1M in mid-June (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/aa/short-interest/, page updated 2026-10-15). That is roughly 4.5% of about 260M shares outstanding: rising, not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is -3.49 vol points, so calls are richer than puts and upside is paid. Put/call open interest is 0.39. ATM IV is 100% on the 1-day expiry and the straddle implies 5.91%. Tape: -6.49% over 5 days, -14.73% over 20 days, -52.2% from the 52-week high. Options lean up, while the stock has sold off hard and shorts have built about 45% since June.

findings.finding: Alumina prices rose through Q3, which helps the alumina segment beyond the company's +$10M sequential outlook, since that outlook holds prices flat. Rio Tinto's Q3 review (2026-10-14) says FOB Australia alumina rose 8% during Q3 to $355/t. Platts puts the Q2 average at $307.42/t, and SMM recorded $346-356/t trades on 5-6 August for September loading. So the Q3 average API was roughly $30-40/t above Q2's. Consensus models third-party alumina sales down 28.8% YoY ($599M, Zacks).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 the alumina segment lost $96M (Pinjarra, energy contracts) and the stock fell 6.13%, a reaction the sweep ties to the alumina guide cut and South32 overhang. Over the 7 prints in the baseline only 2 rose, so good quarter-level news has not reliably been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Alcoa's own Q3 alumina bridge (+$10M) excludes price, and Rio's Q3 review with the quarter-end price landed one day before this print. If this were priced, consensus third-party alumina revenue would not still sit at -28.8% YoY and the stock would not be making new lows on the aluminium price alone. The CFO did say on 10 September that prices had rebounded to about $350, so some analysts will have it.
findings.independence: Platts Q2 average of $307.42/t (https://www.alcircle.com/news/q2-2026-sees-oversupply-weighing-on-fob-australia-alumina-prices-118154) and SMM's $346/t FOB WA trade on 2026-08-06 (https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104049234-30000-mt-alumina-traded-at-346mt-fob-western-australia-for-september-2026-loading) are independent of Rio. The CFO's 'about $350' at Jefferies on 2026-09-10 is the company itself (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aa/transcripts/740953-jefferies-global-industrials-conference-2026/).

findings.finding: LME aluminium cash averaged $3,227/t in Q3 (Westmetall: July 3,156, Aug 3,250, Sep 3,277; Rio says $3,226) against $3,577/t in Q2 (Apr 3,601, May 3,670, Jun 3,459), a fall of about $350/t. On Alcoa's 15-day pricing lag the fall is about $300/t. This is the main reason the bar fell from $2.12 to about $1.50.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From Q1 to Q2 2026, higher prices lifted adjusted EBITDA by $306M (+51%) and EPS still missed; the stock fell 6.13%. A big price-driven swing has not by itself decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the exchange price is public and consensus fell about 14% over 90 days. The only unpriced part is the exact lag effect. The CFO said the 15-day-lag sensitivities miss steep moves near quarter-end, and LME fell sharply in late June, which flatters the start of Q3 realisations. Filed small.
findings.independence: Rio Tinto Q3 review confirms the $3,226 Q3 average (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000863064/000086306426000041/ex1prodresults.htm). The Q2 $3,577 average is in AL Circle/Mysteel, 2026-08-26 (https://www.mysteel.net/news/5138322-eu-canada-and-asia-aluminium-prices-why-3-386t-benchmark-can-cost-5-792t-read-how-regional-premiums-reshaped-markets). The lag comment is in the Q2 call (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aa/transcripts/650444-q2-2026/).

findings.finding: LME aluminium cash has averaged $3,072/t so far in October (Westmetall), about $155/t below the Q3 average and about $205/t below September. SMM and AL Circle describe a fall from $3,248.5 on 28 September to $3,107 on 5 October as the Middle East risk premium unwinding. The Q4 sequential outlook Alcoa gives tonight will carry a price headwind on top of Q3's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sweep says this name trades on the guide and operations. Q2 2026 fell 6.1% on a miss combined with an alumina guide cut. Q1 2026 fell 6.8%. Q3 2025 rose 12.6% on a beat plus a buyback.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (early October; the article covers 28 Sep-5 Oct prices)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is down 14.7% over 20 days and 6.5% over 5 days, which tracks the October metal fall. What is not visible yet is how management frames Q4, including carbon, caustic and the restart costs, against a lower metal price. Sized small because the run-down already reflects much of it.
findings.independence: The Westmetall monthly averages (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=averages&field=LME_Al_cash) are an independent series. AL Circle on the 1 October drop (https://www.alcircle.com/news/lme-aluminium-price-drops-2-62-as-stocks-remain-stable-at-241-375t-on-october-1-121399).

findings.finding: Two dated items set up Q4 alumina tailwinds. Rio Tinto (2026-10-14) says Yarwun output will fall 40% in Q4 2026 on tailings constraints, cutting about 1.2 Mt a year from the Pacific market and supporting the alumina price Alcoa sells at. Separately, Alcoa's CFO said on the Q2 call that caustic, which reaches costs with about a six-month lag, is 'already coming back down', with the benefit landing in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on an alumina-price tailwind in the outlook. The alumina guide cut in Q2 2026 coincided with -6.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Yarwun curtailment was flagged as 'approaching' by the Alcoa CFO on 2026-09-10, but its size (-40% in Q4, about 1.2 Mt annualised) was confirmed in Rio's review only yesterday. If it were priced, alumina-exposed names would have re-rated, and Alcoa has instead fallen on aluminium. The caustic lag is the company's own Q2 statement and is not quantified.
findings.independence: The caustic tailwind is in the Q2 2026 call (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aa/transcripts/650444-q2-2026/), a different document. The CFO's Yarwun mention at Jefferies is at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/alcoa-sees-aluminum-deficit-strong-050200543.html.

findings.finding: At Jefferies on 2026-09-10, ten weeks into the quarter, CFO Molly Beerman said Alcoa was 'carrying great momentum from the second quarter into the third'. She cited production records at five operations continuing into Q3, cash generation 'on track to do the same in the third' as Q2 (Q2 free cash flow was $422M), and a value-add order book 'almost completely sold out for the rest of 2026' with good 2027 premiums expected. The offsets: WA mine approvals 'could slip into 2027', covered by a contingency of about six months, and no buyback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 also came after constructive commentary and missed (EPS $2.12 against about $2.25-2.35), and the stock fell 6.1%. Upbeat intra-quarter tone has not protected this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public webcast, so partly priced. But the stock has fallen about 15% since, almost all of it on the metal price. The operating-momentum and cash statements are company-level and survive a lower LME, and consensus has kept being cut, which suggests analysts are marking to price, not operations.
findings.independence: Reuters via Mining Weekly, 2026-09-11, covering the same appearance (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/cutting-canada-tariffs-alone-wont-flatten-us-aluminum-premium-alcoa-says-2026-09-11). Same event, so not independent.

findings.finding: The US Midwest duty-paid premium averaged $2,420/t in Q3 against $2,406/t in H1 2026 (Rio Tinto), so it was flat over the half. The spot premium was $1.09-1.097/lb on 10-11 September, down from a June record on hopes of a Canada tariff deal. That deal nearly cut the Canadian tariff to 25% before collapsing on 21 August, per the CFO. So the quarter's premium probably eased slightly from Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: The premium is public daily and largely priced. Rio's Q3 average is fresh as of yesterday. Small.
findings.independence: Argus, 2026-08-20: $1.12/lb in August (https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2867643-house-members-seek-probe-into-midwest-premium). Same Rio document as findings 1, 2 and 4, a different line.

findings.finding: Rio Tinto's average realised US tariff cost rose to $1,685/t in Q3 from $1,322/t in H1 2026 ($430M on 255kt), even though LME fell. Alcoa guided its Section 232 cost down $10M sequentially, saying the change is volume only, with no change in rate. It says it pays over $1B a year on about 900kt of Canadian metal at 50%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's per-tonne tariff cost rising is not in any Alcoa preview. It is a proxy: Rio's mix and timing differ, and Alcoa's own guide says volume only, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Alcoa Q2 call, 'No change in the rate, simply volume' (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aa/transcripts/650444-q2-2026/), points the other way. The company document outranks the peer proxy.

findings.finding: South32 shareholders approved the sale of its aluminium assets to Alcoa at the AGM on 2026-10-15, with 99.18% of proxies in favour. The deal is $3.1B cash plus $1.0B in Alcoa shares (17.0M) plus a CVR of up to $750M. It is still subject to regulatory approvals and expected to complete in 2H FY27 / 1H CY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sweep says the deal overhang was cited in the Q2 drop (-6.1%).
findings.why_not_priced: The approval was expected, since the board recommended it and the independent expert found it fair, so it is near zero. It removes one condition, and the call may add regulatory timing.

findings.finding: Alcoa priced $2.6B of senior notes on 2026-09-14: $1.5B at 6.625% due 2034 and $1.1B at 6.875% due 2036, closing 2026-09-23. The proceeds fund the South32 cash consideration and replace the bridge, about 20 months before the expected closing. That adds roughly $44M of gross interest a quarter from Q4, on top of a 5% ticking fee ($80-100M due at closing). What the money buys is an acquisition the company says brings $900M NPV of synergies and pro forma EBITDA of $3.2B, so this is pre-funding, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separable prior. The deal announcement preceded the Q2 drop.
findings.why_not_priced: The coupons are public, but Q4 interest guidance and any negative carry on the cash will appear only in tonight's outlook. Some models may not yet carry about $0.12-0.13 a quarter of pre-tax interest drag before closing.
findings.independence: The CFO at Jefferies confirms the $2.6B issue and the $4.7B pro forma net debt (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aa/transcripts/740953-jefferies-global-industrials-conference-2026/).

findings.finding: Short interest built from about 8.1M (2026-06-15) to 11.7-12.2M (Aug 31-Sep 30), with days to cover up to 2.9-3.5. That comes into a print on a stock 52% off its high and down 14.7% in 20 days, while the options market pays for upside (skew -3.49, put/call OI 0.39).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 rose 12.6% on a beat plus a buyback after a weak run-in. Otherwise 5 of 7 prints fell.
findings.why_not_priced: At about 4.5% of shares it is not crowded, so this is a modest asymmetry, not a squeeze setup. Sized small.
findings.independence: Equibles snapshot, 9.3M / 3.5% float at the July 31 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/aa/short-interest). Same FINRA data.

outside_window.finding: WA mine approvals (federal strategic assessment / state EPA) were originally expected by year-end 2026. The CFO says they 'could slip into 2027', with no financial impact if they arrive by mid-2027.
South32 transaction regulatory approvals and completion in 1H CY2027. The 17.0M Alcoa shares issued to South32 are at least half distributed in specie, and the rest are sold over time as overhang.

San Ciprian, Norway or Iceland energy or curtailment news in Q3 2026: the CFO said 99% of power is covered by contracts and San Ciprian is ramping; nothing negative found

baseline_tension: The mild positive lean agrees with the options market (upside paid, skew -3.49, put/call OI 0.39) but cuts against the reaction history (5 of 7 prints down, the last three -1.5 to -6.8%) and against the October metal fall the 20-day run-down reflects, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): this name has sold 5 of 7 prints, so the reported-quarter positives were cut. Alumina price went from +0.8 to +0.6 and CFO momentum from +0.6 to +0.4. p_up went from 53 to 52.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money buys an acquisition the company says brings $900M NPV of synergies, so it is pre-funding, not distress. The notes finding went from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses): Rio's per-tonne tariff cost is a peer proxy contradicted by Alcoa's own volume-only guide, so it went from -0.2 to -0.1.

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was checked (about 4.5%, 2.9 days to cover, not crowded). The negatives run against an upside-paid skew, so the October LME/Q4 outlook finding went from -0.8 to -0.7.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): two sources agree at $1.49-1.54 and Zacks is at $1.65, so the bar is sourced but dispersed. All sizes were already small; nothing further changed.
